article.description: Sheryl Swoopes scored 15 of her 17 points in the second half and the Houston Comets clinched their seventh straight WNBA playoff berth with a 52-47 victory over the Seattle Storm on Tuesday night.
article.headline: Swoopes, Arcain pace Houston down stretch
article.linkText: Comets clinch seventh straight playoff berth
article.story:
HOUSTON -- Sheryl Swoopes scored 15 of her 17 points in the second half and the Houston Comets clinched their seventh straight WNBA playoff berth with a 52-47 victory over the Seattle Storm on Tuesday night.

Janeth Arcain and Swoopes combined to go 7-for-8 from the free
throw line over the final 1:38 as the Comets improved to 20-11 and
moved within a game of Western Conference leader Los Angeles.

"Whenever I go to the free throw line, I am thinking about just
one thing," Arcain said. "I am alone with the basket and all I
have to do is do what I do in practice. I think we played well at
the end of the game and did what we could to keep them from tying
it."

Seattle (16-15) had a chance to tie the game with 7 seconds
left, but Sue Bird drove toward the basket instead of trying for
the 3-pointer. Her shot was blocked by Michelle Snow and Swoopes
made two free throws to close the scoring.

"I have played a lot of basketball against her and I know what
kind of shots she likes to take," Snow said. "She's one of their
leaders and of course we knew she would have the ball. This win
does take a little pressure off us and now we can focus on getting
ready for the playoffs."

Lauren Jackson had 16 points and 15 rebounds for the Storm,
fifth in the West and a game behind Minnesota and Sacramento. The
top four teams in each conference make the playoffs.

Arcain finished with 14 points and was 6-for-6 from the free
throw line.

Houston took control with a 12-1 run in the second half, moving
ahead 42-33 with 12:23 left in the game.

"We still know we can make the playoffs," Jackson said. "We
have to win tomorrow (in San Antonio). We care too much about each
other as a team to let it slip away like this."
